en: A Praise of the Pure Land of the Mahāyāna, Volume One:

The Dharma-mirror faces the void and reflects; The mind penetrates and the five colors appear. As the manifested mind is pure and wondrously discerns the dharma-realm, it also penetrates [all things];
The wish-fulfilling jewel of the will is ever self-purified; The light of the body illuminates the ten directions.
The sincere mind dwells nowhere; liberation attains purity. Contemplating as if there were no thought, with high voice yet no sound.
Discerning that there is existence where there is no gate. The mirror of wisdom is free from killing; the side-son arises from emptiness and purity.
Awakening, there is nothing upon which to rely; sitting and lying within the dissolution of emptiness.
Transcending those within the realms of humans and devas, I stand for a moment at the edge of the Other Shore.
Having washed away the mud from within my mind, I am pure and free from defilement; May I thereby realize Bodhi. The mirror of wisdom is never obscured by darkness;
The wise always employ its clarity. Though the dust of worldly toil is severed, The treasury of jewels shines forth spontaneously.
The pool refines the golden sands of water, Flowing continuously with the stream of Dharma-nature. Flowers bloom to produce transformed sons who explain their own original roots;
Abiding in thought, one constantly observes. The true King of Treasures of Samādhi revolves through the cycles of the Tripiṭaka;
Do not reject the mud within the mind— If there is someone who single-mindedly recollects the Buddha.
Reciting the Buddha’s name, one enters deep dhyāna; At the first watch of night, sit upright with a focused mind.
The Western Land is before one's eyes; when reciting, know that there is no-thought. This no-thought is suchness itself.
If you can discern this meaning within, it is called the excellence of the Dharma-nature. The Pure Land resides within the heart; the foolish seek it outwardly.
Within the depths lies a precious mirror; If one fails to recognize it, one’s life passes in vain. The Buddhas reside within the heart, yet such a treasure cannot be sought by ordinary means.
How wondrous and rare is this spirit! Hasten your hands and practice with diligence early on.
Everyone possesses this precious mirror, Yet the foolish do not know how to polish it; They are unable to turn their hands to reflect upon themselves.

Dust and grime are ever more abundant; Who among people possesses a precious mirror? The wise person understands how to polish it with diligent effort, Reflecting upon themselves so that dust and grime do not come to defile them.
When the mind is distinct from the constant, one penetrates the self-nature which is fundamentally [empty].
This is the practice of those who realize the principle: To recite the Buddha’s name is itself non-arising.
Crushed ore is not yet gold; within the ore, gold does not appear. Only when one knows how to refine it through smelting can true gold be seen within the crucible.
Contemplating the Buddha as empty and beyond thought, True Suchness is quiescent and speaks not.
To speak of the teachings in words and letters Is but the dhyāna of delusive thoughts in this realm. Nirvāṇa is the ultimate treasury of the Dharma.
Secretly transmitted without being shared; the mind-essence is for one’s own use.
Its majesty shall deliver those with whom there is a karmic affinity—those of the Three Vehicles do not recognize it, and non-Buddhists have never heard of it.
With a slight resentment toward those who slander it much, I vow that it shall not be spread recklessly. The Way is profound and noble; do not rashly attempt to transmit it.
The Way does not favor the worthy; mother and son must not transmit it to one another.
